newsitem.title: BELARUS: Americans, Germans freed after arrest in Belarus.
newsitem.headline: Americans, Germans freed after arrest in Belarus.

text.p: Four foreigners, two Americans and two Germans, were briefly detained during a protest in Belarus against President Alexander Lukashenko, state television said on Saturday.
A journalist arrested with three of the four foreigners on Friday said they had been released after several hours.
"Several people were arrested, including two American and two German citizens, for active participation in the protest," the television news said, quoting the interior ministry.

Russia's Interfax news agency said the four were language students and named them as James Traynor and Karen Dorothy from the United States and Fabian Frenzel and Tim Kochler of Germany (Eds: all spellings approximated from Russian alphabet).
No confirmation of their identities was available.
The journalist, Roman Yakovlevsky, said one of the Americans worked for an international centre on cultural affairs in Minsk and the Germans were working for a student newspaper.
"We were held for a few hours. They took our fingerprints, filmed us and let us go," Yakovlevsky said.
They were released after representatives of the U.S. and German embassies visited the regional police headquarters, Interfax said. Embassy officials were not available for comment.
Reuters correspondents saw about 50 people being bundled into lorries and police vehicles at Friday's protest.
The demonstrators had intended to proceed through the city, a move banned by the authorities.
Some protesters were beaten and looked dazed but there was no sign of bloodshed as police moved in to break up a gathering of up to 2,000 mostly young people.
Other journalists who had been detained at the rally also said they were held for a few hours and then released.

Lukashenko, facing growing unrest among opposition forces, has ordered restrictions on political meetings and banned his opponents from using post-independence national symbols, which he has scrapped in favour of old Soviet ones.
The United States said on Friday it had downgraded its relationship with Belarus because of what it called a "serious turn for the worse" in the human rights situation.
Washington is concerned at plans for closer ties between Russia and Belarus which Russian President Boris Yeltsin said on Friday could even extend to a full merger one day.
